source.title: Mapping fMRI Signal and Image Stimuli in an Artificial Neural Network Latent Space: Bringing Artificial and Natural Minds Together
source.authors: C. M. Dalbagno; Manuel de Castro Ribeiro Jardim; Mihnea Angheluta

record.tranche_reason: Extends representational-similarity analysis to a comparison between an fMRI-trained autoencoder and an image-pretrained ViT, but does not test any version's model-to-model or scale trend directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports one RSA result for fMRI and image representations. This is an adjacent artificial-versus-natural representation comparison, not a comparison of independently trained models. It does not sweep model scale or capability, test vision-language alignment, or complete the proposed latent-space mapping/model stitching.
record.test_reason: The study runs one RSA between a convolutional autoencoder trained on fMRI activation images and a pretrained ViT-base on the matching image stimuli. It motivates this with the convergent-learning literature (it cites arXiv:1511.07543), but no version of the claim is about a model trained on brain data against a vision model. It has no scale or capability sweep (V1) and no vision-language pairing (V2). It has no seeds (V3), no completed mapping or stitching (V4), no feature matching (V5) and no comparison of metrics or inputs (V6, V7). Its one result is an adjacent construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version. The reader's 'tests'/T3 contradicts its own finding that every version is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude the two latent spaces are not correlated and say their hypothesis 'proved untrue'. They call the findings preliminary and inconclusive. They attribute the result possibly to ViT ImageNet pretraining bias, their preprocessing, the AE architecture, and limited time and compute.
record.recipe_differences: Uses RSA on an fMRI autoencoder and an image-pretrained ViT; it does not test a scale trend. The proposed latent-space translation and model stitching were not completed.

fits_no_version.finding: RSA between an fMRI-trained convolutional autoencoder's latents (38 SVD dimensions) and ViT-base in21k image embeddings (715 SVD dimensions) on BOLD5000 gave r = 0.0167.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representations from a model trained on fMRI activation images and from an image-pretrained ViT show near-zero RSA alignment on matched stimuli.

record.problems: The study compares only one fMRI-trained autoencoder and one pretrained ViT, with no control comparison or alternative similarity measure. The authors note limitations in preprocessing, architecture, time, and computational resources. The text's description of the result as non-significant conflicts with its reported p < 0.001.

untested.parts: No scale or capability comparison; only one AE–ViT pair.
No language model and no image–caption pairs.
No same-architecture models from different seeds.
Latent-space translation and model stitching were planned but not done.
No interpretable features or circuits compared.
A single RSA setup with Pearson correlation and TruncatedSVD; no alternative measures or input sets.
No test of plateau or of shared data or objectives as an explanation.

record.verdict_notes: This is a small preliminary student-workshop preprint with one model pair and no controls or null baseline. The 'non-significant' wording conflicts with the reported p < 0.001. With r = 0.017 over roughly 12 million matrix entries, a significant p is unsurprising and practically meaningless. Treat the result as weak evidence even for the adjacent construct.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability comparison and no comparison between independently trained models.
The comparison is fMRI and image representations, not vision and language models on paired images and captions.
No models trained from different initializations are compared.
Latent-space translation and model stitching were proposed but not achieved.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified or compared.
Only one RSA setup is reported; the study does not compare similarity measures, settings, or input distributions.
The study does not test model-to-model convergence, plateaus, or shared training data/objectives as an explanation.

rows.subject: fMRI convolutional autoencoder vs google/vit-base-patch16-224-in21k
rows.stage_stated: Autoencoder trained on fMRI; ViT pretrained on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared the Pearson correlations of dissimilarity matrices for fMRI and image embeddings using RSA.

conditions.value: matched image stimuli and fMRI data
TruncatedSVD; fMRI embeddings reduced to 38 dimensions and image embeddings to 715 dimensions

rows.measure: Pearson correlation between the fMRI and image dissimilarity matrices (RSA)
rows.note: The authors describe the representations as not correlated and elsewhere call the correlation non-significant, despite reporting p < 0.001. The reported correlation is close to zero.
rows.check: Linking to 'none' is correct. The state 'absent' is acceptable: r = 0.0167, which the authors call 'not correlated' and 'no significant correlation'. However, the paper also reports p < 0.001, which contradicts 'non-significant'. The reported r(4999) degrees of freedom are unexplained given about 4,916 stimuli. No baseline or null comparison is reported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
